title: intent claude upgrade --apply appends single-* .prettierignore patterns a file's ** patterns already cover, so every run dirties the tree
body:
Reported 2026-10-23 by rhadamanth-sysadm and, at hv's request, by gyges-sysadm, during the gyges move (Molt ST0006 WP04). Filed by vc from their reports.

## What

`intent claude upgrade --apply` appends three single-`*` `.prettierignore` patterns to a file whose existing `**` patterns already cover them, so every run dirties the tree. Reproduced in `~/Devel/prj/Molt` at e9e37f8 from a clean tree, on gyges with Homebrew's intent 3.2.5 (2e0e9215d) and 3.2.4 (f89b8285) before it, and on rhadamanth with 3.2.5 from `~/.local/bin` as a dry run:

```
intent claude upgrade
would exclude: intent/st/*/info.md in .prettierignore
would exclude: intent/st/*/acceptance.md in .prettierignore
would exclude: intent/st/*/WP/*/info.md in .prettierignore
dry run: 0 would be written, 12 already canonical, 2 preserved, 0 held, 0 skipped.
```

With `--apply` it reports `ok: 0 written, 12 already canonical, 2 preserved, 0 held, 0 skipped.` and `excluded:` for the same three, and `git status` then shows ` M .prettierignore`: after the existing `intent/whiteboard/*/inbox.*.md` line it appends a blank line, the three-line comment headed "Generated views have ONE writer, and it is the renderer", and the three patterns. On the next run it appends them again.

## Why it is wrong

Molt's `.prettierignore` already carries `intent/st/**/info.md` and `intent/st/**/acceptance.md` (lines 29 and 30), under its own comment (lines 26 to 28): "`**` IS LOAD-BEARING: in .prettierignore a single `*` does not cross a `/`, so `intent/st/*/info.md` matches a flat layout and misses every thread under a status directory." The upgrade's coverage check does not count a `**` pattern as covering the single-`*` one it would add, so it adds the narrower, redundant lines on every run.

## Cost

A dirty Molt checkout stops `molt upgrade` before it runs (WP04 runbook P4). Workaround on gyges: `git checkout -- .prettierignore` after each upgrade; nothing is committed.

## Spec (vc, 2026-10-23)

LANE: ic, S, after 0623's close; rides 3.2.6 if its run fits before the cut, else the next patch. SHAPE: the upgrade's `.prettierignore` step judges coverage by what a pattern matches, not by the line's text: a pattern already in the file that matches every path the canon pattern matches covers it, so `intent/st/**/info.md` covers `intent/st/*/info.md` and nothing is appended; the step keeps adding a pattern a file lacks. The lane also measures whether the canon's own single-`*` patterns miss a layout Intent supports (a thread realised under a status directory); if they do, the canon emits the `**` form and says so in the CHANGELOG line. PROOF: an arm with a scratch project whose `.prettierignore` carries Molt's `**` lines: the dry run prints no `would exclude`, `--apply` writes nothing and the tree stays clean, red on the base; the existing arm that adds the patterns to a file lacking them stays green; one arm per form the coverage reads (`*`, `**`, a literal path). CLOSES WHEN: the bank is judged and landed and `intent issues close 0633` names the sha; the live confirmation is gyges-sysadm's repro on the first brew carrying the fix, which the record notes when it comes.

## Resolution

Fixed by 6a3f9aaef for 3.2.6 (refs/bank/ic/0633/fix.patch, patch-id 49eedf8ae5dd, landed on vc's word after 0630's fix): the upgrade's `.prettierignore` step judges coverage by what a line matches, through the `ignore` crate's gitignore matcher, not by the line's text. Each canon pattern is probed once, with its `*` replaced by a private-use character, and a line that matches the probe or any of its parents covers it, so `intent/st/**/info.md` covers both `intent/st/*/info.md` and `intent/st/*/WP/*/info.md`, and `intent/st/**/acceptance.md` covers `intent/st/*/acceptance.md`. Molt's file carries two `**` lines, not the three vc's spec message counted, and between them they cover every pattern the upgrade appended. A line carrying `?`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}` or a backslash, and every `!` line, counts only by its exact text, as every line did before, because globset reads braces as alternation where prettier reads them literally. THE MEASUREMENT THE SPEC ASKED FOR: the canon's single-`*` patterns miss no layout Intent supports, because v3 realises a thread only at the flat `intent/st/<ID>/` path (`Project::thread_dir`), migration leaves a v2 bucket copy unrendered, and organize holds a thread rather than realising it beside a bucket copy; so the canon keeps its form and the CHANGELOG line says nothing of it. PROOF: arms in agents_sync_parity.rs, one per form the coverage reads (`**`, `*`, a literal path) and a control for a line the probe cannot judge, beside the unchanged arm that adds the patterns to a file lacking them. The `**` arm is the spec's Molt case: its dry run prints no `would exclude`, and `--apply` leaves `.prettierignore` byte-identical and the tree clean. On cc's combined runs over the composed trees, with the facade hunk reversed the `**`, `*` and literal arms failed at their coverage assertions and the control stayed green; with the fix every arm passed, and the whole intentsvcs and intent-cli suites, fmt, clippy and doc were green, as was the whole shell half on the final composition. The live confirmation is gyges-sysadm's repro on the first brew carrying the fix, which this record notes when it comes.
